Built to Run

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 51% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

The Offensive Blueprint

They spread the ball as much as anyone — the WR1 commands only 19% of targets (league ~23%). Volume is democratic here, which suppresses any single receiver's ceiling but props up the TE and secondary options.

They lean on tempo — a 16% no-huddle rate (league ~11%) that inflates snap counts and everyone's volume.

By the numbers it's a struggling unit — a 41% success rate (below the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (48% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — Soft on the Ground

They surrender 132 rushing and 224 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 51 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.68/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak WR1 receiving TDs (0.47/game vs ~0.38) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
